I went a little overboard last year and used live champagne yeast with a Christmas Ale kit I got from Northern Brewer. The batch was outstanding, however the beer tended to, well, act like champagne and explode out the bottle. Lost a few bottles this way and had to repaint my kitchen ceiling.

The alcohol content was very high, but could I achieve the same abv with a less excitable yeast?

The type of yeast really doesn't have much to do with the eruptions you're experiencing. You either bottled it to early, didn't adjust the priming sugar to the quantity of beer, or a combination of both. For example you used the 5 oz. bag they sent, but had less than 5 gallons of beer . That being said, many styles of beer yeast can ferment up to fairly high ABV's with proper aeration, and nutrients. The "White Labs WLP099 Super High Gravity Ale" strain says it can go to 25%.

It could be possible to achieve a similar content without the carb.

I can't speak from experience, but I'd imagine a wine or mead yeast would do something similar to what you are looking for, as champagne yeast is suggested for any "sparkling" variety.

Wyeast makes a dry mead/sweet mead yeast strain(s), that would likely be your best bet, but I am not speaking from experience, as I'm currently 1 month into my first mead.

I'm looking for an android device to use as a bike computer, and specifically not using my Nexus 6. I'm a battery destroyer already, and even adding my battery packs into the mix I can still manage to kill my battery on a longer ride, especially since I'll hit areas with little to no cell service. So what I'd like is a different phone device to use that could do a better job, and be a more permanent fixture on my bike.

Here is what it would need:

  • BT 4.0 LE support
  • Long lasting battery life (the display will be on basically the entire time, though likely very low brightness)
  • Smaller display is a positive
  • Good community/dev support is a major plus. I don't need latest & greatest, but recent & stable with all hardware bits working.

This is basically an alternative solution to using my Nexus 6 with a RFLKT/RFLKT+ and an external battery pack. I'll be using this device with:

  • Wahoo SC Speed & Cadence Sensor
  • External GPS such as a Garmin GLO (I want more accuracy than what a phone is going to give me, haven't decided on a unit though)
  • Mio Link HRM

I'm not using any ANT devices, so I don't really care if the phone has one.

Thanks for any help / ideas! Its this or I'm going to just buy a Garmin Edge 520, but I'd rather go with an Android device :)
Android device as bike computer - but not my phone

With the 520 on the horizon, and as a cyclist, I would advocate for that: To completely have your phone for other uses such as in the case of an emergency. As you mentioned, the 520 will have better GPS than any phone, due to the inclusion of GLONASS. 15 hour battery life. Real time Strava inclusion. Ability to pair with ANT devices. Still no maps though :(

And no ability to work with bluetooth sensors despite what it seemed at first, making it unfortunately quite useless for me.

I have a very accurate HRM, why should I buy another just because Garmin doesn't want to budge from ANT? Frankly, buying an external GPS would be much more cost effective and give me equal or greater accuracy. The Nexus 4 I'm currently using as a test subject also uses GLONASS, though it is still less accurate than a good external.

As of right now, Garmin is at the bottom of the list for me. Polar may have something, but I'm not sure if the value is there. With no cellular use, disabling the radio, tethering to my Nexus 6 for data, a custom rom, kernel, and no apps other than those required, with the screen on the entire time, I'm looking at several days of battery life.

I may just buy a new phone mount this weekend. If only Strava would show current speed/cadence, I'd be happy. I may hack something together for that by itself.

Edit: And this is a standalone device, my phone is my phone and is being kept separate, so emergency is a non-issue.
